description: Itiner-e: A high-resolution dataset of roads of the Roman Empire is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Pau de Soto et al. The Roman Empire’s road system was critical for structuring the movement of people, goods and ideas, and sustaining imperial control. Yet, it remains incompletely mapped and poorly integrated across sources despite centuries of research. We present Itiner-e, the most detailed and complete open digital dataset of roads in the entire Roman Empire. Coverage: not stated; published in 2025. Formats: Shapefile, GeoJSON, GeoPackage. The data are held in Zenodo and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC BY 4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
